characters.note: Consulting detective; disguises himself as a drunken groom and as a Nonconformist clergyman.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator, Holmes's friend and former lodger, recently married.

characters.note: Barrister of the Inner Temple, Irene's lover and later husband.

brief.place: London: Baker Street lodgings, Serpentine Avenue in St. John's Wood, Edgeware Road, the Inner Temple; the King's Bohemia is referenced but not shown.
brief.dress: Holmes in tweed suits and disguises (a shabby drunken groom, an amiable Nonconformist clergyman with broad black hat and white tie); Watson in Victorian civilian dress with ulster and top-hat; the King in rich Continental attire with astrakhan-trimmed coat, blue cloak lined with flame-coloured silk, fur-topped boots, and a black vizard mask; Irene in evening dress or walking clothes.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Baker Street rooms with fireplace, armchairs, cigar case, spirit case and gasogene; Briony Lodge with a sitting-room with long windows and a sliding panel above the bell-pull; a landau and brougham with pairs of horses; pink-tinted notepaper watermarked with E, g, P, G, t; a cabinet-size photograph; a smoke-rocket; an emerald snake ring; a gold watch.
depiction_rules: The King should be shown masked in the first meeting and unmasked only after he tears the mask off.
Irene Adler is always the woman, shown beautiful and self-possessed; in the brawl she is in the doorway with her figure outlined against the hall lights.
Holmes's disguises should be visibly different from his usual appearance; he is never shown in his own face during disguises.
Show the smoke and street crowd as a chaotic brawl with men struggling, not as a clean scene.
